name: RRI
description: RRI returns the compound annual growth rate (CAGR) that grows an investment from a present value to a future value over a number of periods.
tldr: Calculates the equivalent compound interest rate for an investment.

basicExample.description: Annual growth rate of an investment
basicExample.explanation: An investment that grew from $10,000 to $15,000 over 5 years had an annual growth rate of about 8.45%.

advancedExamples.title: CAGR over years
advancedExamples.description: Compound annual growth rate for a stock
advancedExamples.explanation: The stock grew at a compound annual rate of about 9.14% over 10 years.

howItWorks: RRI uses the formula (fv / pv)^(1/nper) - 1 to compute the equivalent compound growth rate. It is the inverse of the future-value formula.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Requires pv and fv to have the same sign.
Result is the periodic rate, not annual unless periods are years.
Does not account for dividends or additional contributions.

commonErrors.cause: pv is zero or negative, or fv and pv have opposite signs.
commonErrors.fix: Use positive pv and fv, with fv > pv for growth.

commonErrors.cause: nper is in months but result was interpreted as annual.
commonErrors.fix: Use annual periods for annual CAGR, or multiply the monthly rate by 12.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: RRI works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between RRI and IRR?
faq.answer: RRI is for a single starting and ending value. IRR is for a series of cash flows.

faq.question: Can RRI calculate CAGR?
faq.answer: Yes, RRI is essentially the CAGR formula.
